idiom_name: function-valued prop invoked as render(state) or children(state)
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the mechanism is simply a function prop: the React documentation defines a render prop as 'a function prop that a component uses to know what to render', notes that any prop returning elements qualifies - the conventional render={...} prop and the children-as-a-function spelling are the same thing - and records that many cases have since been replaced by custom Hooks. Keep the render prop when the owner must be part of the tree (it can hold context, refs or a portal that a hook cannot provide) and use a hook when only state or logic is shared. Vue's scoped slots are the same mechanism in template form: the child passes data to a slot outlet and the parent's slot content receives it as slot props, which the docs compare directly to a function being passed into the child component.
pitfalls: The render function is a new value on every parent render, so memoized owners and heavy children under the callback re-render even when the state is unchanged.
children-as-a-function is invisible to prop checking unless declared, so a consumer passing a node where a function is expected fails at render time.
The function must stay pure rendering of the state it receives; using it for side effects or data pulls turns the pattern into an accidental lifecycle hook.
Nesting several render-prop owners recreates a callback pyramid that hook calls flatten.

variants.name: Vue scoped slots (slot props as the render function)
variants.idiom_name: <slot :item="state" /> with v-slot="{ item }" in the parent template
variants.implementation_notes: Vue realizes the pattern through scoped slots: the child renders <slot :text="hello" :count="1" /> and the parent receives those props in its slot content (v-slot="{ text, count }"), so the child owns the state while the parent authors the markup. The docs state that you can think of a scoped slot as a function being passed into the child component and show the equivalent JavaScript form, in which the slot is a function the child calls with its props. Use it when the rendering must stay in the template (directives, fallthrough behaviour, SSR); the Composition API composable is the hook equivalent and should be preferred when only logic is shared.
variants.code_sketch: cursor at {{ x }},{{ y }}
pitfalls: Slot content is compiled in the parent's scope, so the child's internal state is reachable only through slot props; expecting the child's scope silently fails.
Scoped slots are functions under the hood, so an inline slot body is recreated per render exactly like an inline React render prop - the same memoization cost applies.
With named scoped slots every slot prop set must be bound explicitly; a component expecting a function-valued default slot renders nothing if the call site binds the wrong slot.
